meals.name: Protein Oat Bowl with Boiled Eggs
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Hard-boil the 2 eggs in boiling water for 9 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.
Step 2: While the eggs cook, combine 60g oats with 120ml water in a small pot and simmer 3-4 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
Step 3: Transfer the oats to a bowl and stir in the 150g greek yogurt.
Step 4: Slice the banana on top and serve with the eggs on the side.

meals.name: Chicken, Broccoli and White Rice Bowl
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Cook the white rice according to package directions and keep warm.
Step 2: Cut the chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and season with salt and pepper.
Step 3: Cook the chicken in a dry non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Step 4: Steam the broccoli florets for 4-5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Step 5: Serve the chicken and broccoli over the rice.

meals.name: Chicken and Egg Fried Rice
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Cut the chicken breast into small cubes and season with salt and pepper.
Step 2: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5-6 minutes until cooked through; set aside.
Step 3: Chop the broccoli into small florets and steam for 3 minutes, then add to the pan.
Step 4: Push the vegetables aside, crack in the egg and scramble until just set, then mix everything together.
Step 5: Add the cooked white rice and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until heated through, then season with salt and pepper to taste.

results.note: Fridge has chicken; vegetarian user must never get it.

meals.name: Tofu, Spinach and Pepper Rice Bowl
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Cook the brown rice according to the package directions, or use 150g of pre-cooked rice.
Step 2: Cut the tofu into 2cm cubes and pat dry with a paper towel.
Step 3: Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the tofu cubes for 6-8 minutes, turning until golden on all sides.
Step 4: Slice the bell pepper into strips and add to the pan for 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Step 5: Add the spinach and toss for 1-2 minutes until just wilted.
Step 6: Serve the tofu and vegetables over the brown rice in a bowl.

meals.name: Egg and Spinach Scramble with Tofu and Brown Rice
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Cook the brown rice according to the package directions, or use 100g of pre-cooked rice.
Step 2: Dice the bell pepper and crumble the tofu into small pieces.
Step 3: Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and cook the bell pepper and tofu for 4-5 minutes until the pepper softens and the tofu lightly browns.
Step 4: Add the spinach and stir for 1 minute until wilted.
Step 5: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pour into the pan. Stir gently for 2-3 minutes until just set.
Step 6: Serve the scramble alongside the brown rice.

meals.name: Sweet Potato and Avocado Kale Hash
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Dice the sweet potato into 1 cm cubes.
Step 2: Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and add the sweet potato. Cover and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and lightly browned.
Step 3: Chop the kale finely, add it to the pan and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until wilted.
Step 4: Slice the avocado half and serve on top of the hash.

meals.name: Quinoa Chickpea Kale Bowl
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Rinse the quinoa, then simmer it in 150ml water for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
Step 2: Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then pat them dry.
Step 3: Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat, add the chickpeas and cook for 5 minutes until lightly crisp.
Step 4: Massage the chopped kale with a pinch of salt for 1 minute, then add it to the pan for 2 minutes.
Step 5: Combine the quinoa, chickpeas and kale in a bowl and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice if available.

meals.name: Roasted Sweet Potato, Chickpea and Kale Tray
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Step 2: Cut the sweet potato into wedges and toss with half the olive oil, salt and pepper. Roast for 20 minutes.
Step 3: Drain and pat dry the chickpeas, toss with the remaining olive oil and add to the tray. Roast for another 15 minutes until crisp.
Step 4: Tear the kale into pieces, add it to the tray for the last 5 minutes of roasting and toss everything together before serving.

meals.name: Salmon and Avocado Spinach Salad
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Pan-sear the salmon over medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes per side until cooked through, then let it rest for 2 minutes and flake or slice it.
Step 2: Rinse the spinach and place it in a bowl.
Step 3: Halve the avocado, remove the stone, and slice the flesh.
Step 4: Top the spinach with the salmon and avocado slices, then finish with lemon juice, salt and pepper if desired.

meals.name: Salmon, Zucchini and Egg Scramble
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Dice the zucchini into small cubes and cut the salmon into bite-sized pieces.
Step 2: Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and cook the zucchini for 4-5 minutes until tender.
Step 3: Add the salmon and cook for 2 minutes, breaking it up gently.
Step 4: Whisk the eggs, pour them into the pan, and stir gently until just set.
Step 5: Fold in the spinach and cook for 1 minute until wilted. Season and serve.

meals.name: Protein Scramble with Cottage Cheese
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Crack the 3 eggs into a bowl and whisk with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Step 2: Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat.
Step 3: Pour in the eggs and stir gently with a spatula for 2-3 minutes until just set but still soft.
Step 4: Remove from heat, fold in the 150g cottage cheese, and serve warm.

meals.name: Beef and Black Bean Potato Hash
ingredients: Salt, pepper, and paprika to taste
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Microwave the diced potato for 4-5 minutes, or boil it for 8-10 minutes, until fork-tender.
Step 2: Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Step 3: Add the ground beef, season with salt, pepper, and paprika, and cook 6-8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Step 4: Add the potato and black beans, stir, and cook another 4-5 minutes until heated through and lightly crisped.
Step 5: Adjust seasoning and serve hot.

meals.name: Garlic Chicken with Broccoli and Steamed Rice
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Cook the white rice according to package directions until tender, then keep warm.
Step 2: Pat the chicken breast dry, season both sides with salt and pepper, and slice it into thin strips or medallions.
Step 3: Finely chop the garlic cloves.
Step 4: Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden and cooked through (internal temperature 74°C / 165°F). Transfer to a plate.
Step 5: Lower the heat to medium, add the garlic to the same pan and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Step 6: Add the broccoli florets with 2 tbsp water, cover and steam for 4 to 5 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp.
Step 7: Return the chicken to the pan, toss with the garlic and broccoli, and season with salt and pepper.
Step 8: Serve the chicken and broccoli over the warm rice.

meals.name: Lentil and Carrot Stew
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Dice the onion and chop the carrots into small pieces.
Step 2: Heat the olive oil in a small pot over medium heat and sauté the onion for 3 to 4 minutes until soft.
Step 3: Add the carrots and cumin, and stir for 1 minute.
Step 4: Add the cooked lentils and water or stock. Bring to a simmer.
Step 5: Simmer uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes, until the carrots are tender and the stew has thickened.
Step 6: Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.

meals.name: Tomato and Egg Scramble
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Dice the tomato into small pieces.
Step 2: Beat the 2 eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Step 3: Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Step 4: Add the diced tomato and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until softened.
Step 5: Pour in the beaten eggs and gently stir with a spatula for 2 to 3 minutes until just set but still soft.
Step 6: Serve immediately.

meals.name: Banana Oatmell Bowl
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Bring 250ml water to a simmer in a small saucepan.
Step 2: Stir in 80g oats and cook over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Step 3: Slice the banana into rounds and stir half into the oats, reserving the rest for topping.
Step 4: Transfer to a bowl, top with the remaining banana slices, and serve warm.

meals.name: Chicken and Rice Bowl
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Cook the white rice according to package directions until tender, then keep warm.
Step 2: Pat the chicken breast dry and slice it into thin strips or cubes.
Step 3: Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and cooked through (internal temperature 74C).
Step 4: Serve the chicken over the rice in a bowl.

meals.name: Herb-Free Chicken and Rice Plate
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Cook the white rice according to package directions until tender.
Step 2: Season the chicken breast with a pinch of salt and pepper if available.
Step 3: Cook the chicken in a non-stick pan over medium heat for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through (internal temperature 74C).
Step 4: Rest the chicken for 3 minutes, slice, and serve with the rice.

meals.name: Banana Oatmeal with Milk
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Combine 60g oats and 250ml milk in a small pot over medium heat.
Step 2: Stir for 5 minutes until thick and creamy.
Step 3: Slice the banana on top and serve.

meals.name: Soy Chicken Fried Rice with Egg and Broccoli
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Cook 80g white rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, then drain.
Step 2: Dice the chicken into small cubes and sear in a hot pan for 5 minutes until cooked through.
Step 3: Add the minced garlic, broccoli and spinach and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Step 4: Push the vegetables aside, scramble the egg in the pan, then add the rice and soy sauce and toss for 2 minutes.

meals.name: Garlic Tomato Chicken with Spinach and Cheddar Rice
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Cook 80g white rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, then drain and keep warm.
Step 2: Slice the chicken into strips and cook in a hot pan for 5 minutes until golden.
Step 3: Add the minced garlic and chopped tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes until saucy.
Step 4: Stir in the spinach and soy sauce until wilted, then top with the grated cheddar and serve over the rice.

meals.name: Spinach, Egg and Sweet Potato Breakfast Bowl with Greek Yogurt
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Scrub the sweet potato, prick it with a fork, and microwave on high for 6-8 minutes until soft, or bake at 200°C for 30-35 minutes. Cut into cubes once cool enough to handle.

Step 3: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt. Pour into the same pan over medium-low heat and stir gently until just set, about 3-4 minutes.
Step 4: Spoon the Greek yogurt into a bowl. Top with the sweet potato cubes, scrambled eggs and wilted spinach. Serve immediately.

meals.name: Chicken, Brown Rice and Broccoli Spinach Bowl
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Cook the brown rice according to package directions until tender, then keep warm.
Step 2: Cut the chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and season with salt, pepper and paprika if available.
Step 3: Cook the chicken in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and cooked through (internal temperature 74°C).
Step 4: Cut the broccoli into small florets and steam for 4-5 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp.

meals.name: Roasted Chicken, Sweet Potato and Broccoli Brown Rice Plate
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Peel and cube the sweet potatoes into 2 cm pieces and spread on a lined tray.
Step 2: Roast the sweet potato for 20-25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.
Step 3: Season the chicken breast with salt, pepper and garlic powder if available. Pan-sear over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes per side until cooked through (internal temperature 74°C), then rest for 3 minutes and slice.

Step 5: Steam the broccoli florets for 4-5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Step 6: Plate the rice with the sliced chicken, roasted sweet potato and broccoli. Serve warm.

meals.name: Spinach and Mushroom Egg Scramble
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Wipe the mushrooms and slice them thinly. Rinse the spinach and drain it well.

meals.name: Tofu, Zucchini and Bell Pepper Rice Bowl
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Cook the brown rice according to package directions, about 35 minutes, then keep warm.
Step 2: Press the tofu between paper towels for 5 minutes, then cut it into 2 cm cubes.
Step 3: Dice the zucchini and bell pepper into bite-sized pieces.
Step 4: Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add the tofu and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, turning until golden on all sides. Season with salt and pepper.

meals.name: Mushroom, Spinach and Tofu Stir-Fry with Zucchini
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
meals.recipe:
Step 1: Cook the brown rice according to package directions, about 35 minutes, then keep warm.
Step 2: Press the tofu between paper towels for 5 minutes, then cut it into cubes. Slice the onion, bell pepper, zucchini and mushrooms into bite-sized pieces.

Step 4: Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes. Add the mushrooms, bell pepper and zucchini and stir-fry for 5 to 6 minutes.
Step 5: Return the tofu to the pan, add the spinach, and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted. Season with salt and pepper and serve over the rice.

workouts.name: Beginner Full-Body Strength
workouts.description: Full-body strength work builds muscle, which raises your resting calorie burn, and it is gentle enough to start from a sedentary baseline. Each exercise uses large muscle groups for efficient fat-loss training.
workouts.warmup: 5 min easy walking in place or marching, 10 arm circles each direction, 10 bodyweight squats at a slow pace, 10 hip circles each side.
workouts.cooldown: 5 min slow walking, then hold each stretch 30 seconds: child's pose, hamstring stretch, and chest opener against a wall.

exercises.name: Incline Push-Up
exercises.formTip: Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels and lower your chest toward the edge of the surface.
exercises.notes: Use a bench or sturdy counter. Make it easier by raising the surface higher.
instructions: Stand facing bench or sturdy elevated platform. Place hands on edge of bench or platform, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Position forefoot back from bench or platform with arms and body straight. Arms should be perpendicular to body. Keeping body straight, lower chest to edge of box or platform by bending arms.
Push body up until arms are extended. Repeat.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Rows
exercises.formTip: Keep your chest tall and pull the handle toward your lower ribs while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
exercises.notes: Avoid rocking your torso back and forth to move the weight.
instructions: For this exercise you will need access to a low pulley row machine with a V-bar. Note: The V-bar will enable you to have a neutral grip where the palms of your hands face each other. To get into the starting position, first sit down on the machine and place your feet on the front platform or crossbar provided making sure that your knees are slightly bent and not locked.
Lean over as you keep the natural alignment of your back and grab the V-bar handles.

With your arms extended pull back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle from your legs. Your back should be slightly arched and your chest should be sticking out. You should be feeling a nice stretch on your lats as you hold the bar in front of you. This is the starting position of the exercise.

Keeping the torso stationary, pull the handles back towards your torso while keeping the arms close to it until you touch the abdominals. Breathe out as you perform that movement. At that point you should be squeezing your back muscles hard. Hold that contraction for a second and slowly go back to the original position while breathing in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.weight: Light kettlebell or dumbbell, about 10-15 lb
exercises.formTip: Hold the weight close to your chest, push your hips back and down, and keep your heels planted.
exercises.notes: Squat only as deep as you can control with a neutral spine.
instructions: Stand holding a light kettlebell by the horns close to your chest. This will be your starting position.
Squat down between your legs until your hamstrings are on your calves. Keep your chest and head up and your back straight.
At the bottom position, pause and use your elbows to push your knees out. Return to the starting position, and repeat for 10-20 repetitions.

exercises.name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.formTip: Drive through your heel and squeeze your glute at the top, keeping your hips level.
exercises.notes: Keep the non-working leg extended or bent with the foot on the floor.
instructions: Lay on the floor with your feet flat and knees bent.
Raise one leg off of the ground, pulling the knee to your chest. This will be your starting position.
Execute the movement by driving through the heel, extending your hip upward and raising your glutes off of the ground.
Extend as far as possible, pause and then return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.formTip: Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
exercises.notes: Drop to your knees if you lose your form.
instructions: Get into a prone position on the floor, supporting your weight on your toes and your forearms. Your arms are bent and directly below the shoulder.
Keep your body straight at all times, and hold this position as long as possible. To increase difficulty, an arm or leg can be raised.

workouts.name: Beginner Treadmill Walk
workouts.description: Steady walking is low-impact, easy to sustain, and burns a meaningful number of calories without overloading a sedentary body. It is a sustainable base for building fat-loss habits.
workouts.warmup: 5 min slow walk at 2.0 mph with gentle arm swings and ankle circles.
workouts.cooldown: 5 min slow walk at 2.0 mph, then calf stretch and hamstring stretch for 30 seconds each side.

exercises.name: Walking, Treadmill
exercises.structure: Walk at 3.0-3.5 mph with a 1% incline. Every 5 min, increase speed by 0.1 mph if you can still talk comfortably. Hold the pace for the final 5 min.
exercises.notes: Use the talk test: you should be able to speak in full sentences. Stop if you feel dizzy or chest discomfort.
instructions: To begin, step onto the treadmill and select the desired option from the menu. Most treadmills have a manual setting, or you can select a program to run. Typically, you can enter your age and weight to estimate the amount of calories burned during exercise. Elevation can be adjusted to change the intensity of the workout.

Treadmills offer convenience, cardiovascular benefits, and usually have less impact than walking outside. When walking, you should move at a moderate to fast pace, not a leisurely one. Being an activity of lower intensity, walking doesn't burn as many calories as some other activities, but still provides great benefit. A 150 lb person will burn about 175 calories walking 4 miles per hour for 30 minutes, compared to 450 calories running twice as fast. Maintain proper posture as you walk, and only hold onto the handles when necessary, such as when dismounting or checking your heart rate.

workouts.name: Beginner Mobility and Recovery
workouts.description: Gentle mobility work improves posture and joint comfort, which helps you stay consistent with training. It is a low-stress session that supports recovery between workouts.
workouts.warmup: 2 min easy breathing in a seated position, then 10 slow cat-cow cycles on hands and knees.
workouts.cooldown: 2 min seated rest with slow nasal breathing and a gentle shoulder roll.

exercises.name: Cat Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Inhale to arch your back, exhale to round your spine.
exercises.notes: Move slowly and keep your wrists under your shoulders.
instructions: Position yourself on the floor on your hands and knees.
Pull your belly in and round your spine, lower back, shoulders, and neck, letting your head drop.
Hold for 15 seconds.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.breathingCue: Breathe deeply into your back, letting it expand on each inhale.
exercises.notes: Widen your knees if your hips feel tight.
instructions: Get on your hands and knees, walk your hands in front of you.
Lower your buttocks down to sit on your heels. Let your arms drag along the floor as you sit back to stretch your entire spine.
Once you settle onto your heels, bring your hands next to your feet and relax. "breathe" into your back. Rest your forehead on the floor. Avoid this position if you have knee problems.

exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor
exercises.breathingCue: Exhale as you gently shift your hips forward.
exercises.notes: Place a cushion under your back knee. Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg to deepen the stretch.
instructions: Kneel on a mat and bring your right knee up so the bottom of your foot is on the floor and extend your left leg out behind you so the top of your foot is on the floor.
Shift your weight forward until you feel a stretch in your hip. Hold for 15 seconds, then repeat for your other side.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Exhale as you hinge forward from your hips.
exercises.notes: Keep a slight bend in the front knee if needed.
instructions: Lie on your back with one leg extended above you, with the hip at ninety degrees. Keep the other leg flat on the floor.
Loop a belt, band, or rope over the ball of your foot. This will be your starting position.
Pull on the belt to create tension in the calves and hamstrings. Hold this stretch for 10-30 seconds, and repeat with the other leg.

exercises.name: Spinal Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Inhale to prepare, exhale as you rotate gently.
exercises.notes: Rotate from your upper back and keep your hips grounded.
instructions: Sit in a chair so your back is straight and your feet planted on the floor.
Interlace your fingers behind your head, elbows out and your chin down.
Twist your upper body to one side about 3 times as far as you can. Then lean forward and twist your torso to reach your elbow to the floor on the inside of your knee.
Return to upright position and then repeat for your other side.

exercises.name: Upward Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Inhale as you reach up, exhale as you relax your shoulders down.
exercises.notes: Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your lower back.
instructions: Extend both hands straight above your head, palms touching.
Slowly push your hands up and back, keeping your back straight.

workouts.name: Pull Strength & Biceps
workouts.description: Your last session was Push Day, so this workout skips chest, shoulders and triceps and focuses on back and biceps. Heavy vertical and horizontal pulling builds back thickness and arm size, which supports your muscle-building goal while your body recovers from pressing work.
workouts.warmup: 5 min light rowing or cycling, then 2 sets of 10 band pull-aparts (no shoulder pressing), 10 bodyweight scap pulls on a bar, and 10 bodyweight rows with a light load.
workouts.cooldown: 5 min easy walking, then Child's Pose for 60 seconds and Spinal Stretch for 60 seconds each side, breathing slowly through the nose.

exercises.name: Pullups
exercises.weight: Bodyweight (add load when 8+ reps are easy)
exercises.formTip: Start each rep from a dead hang, pull your chest toward the bar, and avoid swinging.
exercises.notes: Use a band or assisted machine if you cannot complete 6 reps yet.
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with the palms facing forward using the prescribed grip. Note on grips: For a wide grip, your hands need to be spaced out at a distance wider than your shoulder width. For a medium grip, your hands need to be spaced out at a distance equal to your shoulder width and for a close grip at a distance smaller than your shoulder width.

As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position.

Pull your torso up until the bar touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the full contracted position. The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.
After a second on the contracted position, start to inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row
exercises.formTip: Keep your back flat at roughly 45 degrees and pull the dumbbells toward your hip, not your chest.
exercises.notes: Brace your core throughout.
instructions: With a dumbbell in each hand (palms facing your torso), bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward by bending at the waist; as you bend make sure to keep your back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Tip: Make sure that you keep the head up. The weights should hang directly in front of you as your arms hang perpendicular to the floor and your torso. This is your starting position.

While keeping the torso stationary, lift the dumbbells to your side (as you breathe out), keeping the elbows close to the body (do not exert any force with the forearm other than holding the weights). On the top contracted position, squeeze the back muscles and hold for a second.
Slowly lower the weight again to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Rows
exercises.formTip: Sit tall, pull the handle to your lower ribs, and squeeze your shoulder blades together before extending your arms.
exercises.notes: Avoid leaning back excessively to move the weight.
instructions: For this exercise you will need access to a low pulley row machine with a V-bar. Note: The V-bar will enable you to have a neutral grip where the palms of your hands face each other. To get into the starting position, first sit down on the machine and place your feet on the front platform or crossbar provided making sure that your knees are slightly bent and not locked.
Lean over as you keep the natural alignment of your back and grab the V-bar handles.

With your arms extended pull back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle from your legs. Your back should be slightly arched and your chest should be sticking out. You should be feeling a nice stretch on your lats as you hold the bar in front of you. This is the starting position of the exercise.

Keeping the torso stationary, pull the handles back towards your torso while keeping the arms close to it until you touch the abdominals. Breathe out as you perform that movement. At that point you should be squeezing your back muscles hard. Hold that contraction for a second and slowly go back to the original position while breathing in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
exercises.formTip: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and avoid swinging your torso.
exercises.notes: Supinate your wrists as you curl for full biceps contraction.
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Hammer Curls
exercises.formTip: Keep palms facing each other throughout and control the lowering phase.
exercises.notes: Targets the brachialis and forearms for added arm thickness.
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell on each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
The palms of the hands should be facing your torso. This will be your starting position.

Now, while holding your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the weight forward while contracting the biceps. Continue to raise the weight until the biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief moment as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Focus on keeping the elbow stationary and only moving your forearm.
After the brief pause, inhale and slowly begin the lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

workouts.name: Lower Body Strength
workouts.description: A leg day that fits your very active lifestyle and muscle-building goal. It avoids the chest, shoulders and triceps trained in your last session and provides heavy compound loading for the largest muscles in the body.
workouts.warmup: 5 min bike or treadmill walk, then 10 bodyweight squats, 10 glute bridges, 10 walking lunges, and 2 light sets of Barbell Squat with just the bar.
workouts.cooldown: 5 min walking, then Kneeling Hip Flexor for 60 seconds each side, Hamstring Stretch for 60 seconds each leg, and Child's Pose for 60 seconds.

exercises.name: Barbell Squat
exercises.formTip: Brace your core, keep your knees tracking over your toes, and descend until your hip crease is below your knee.
exercises.notes: Use a spotter or safety pins for heavy sets.
instructions: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack to just below shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. (Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances discussed in the foot stances section).

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and hips as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.formTip: Push your hips back with a slight knee bend and keep the bar close to your legs as you lower it.
exercises.notes: Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch or your back begins to round.
instructions: Put a barbell in front of you on the ground and grab it using a pronated (palms facing down) grip that a little wider than shoulder width. Tip: Depending on the weight used, you may need wrist wraps to perform the exercise and also a raised platform in order to allow for better range of motion.
Bend the knees slightly and keep the shins vertical, hips back and back straight. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your back and arms completely straight at all times, use your hips to lift the bar as you exhale. Tip: The movement should not be fast but steady and under control.

Once you are standing completely straight up, lower the bar by pushing the hips back, only slightly bending the knees, unlike when squatting. Tip: Take a deep breath at the start of the movement and keep your chest up. Hold your breath as you lower and exhale as you complete the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.formTip: Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes at the top, keeping your ribs down.
exercises.notes: Hold the top position for one second on each rep.
instructions: Begin seated on the ground with a bench directly behind you. Have a loaded barbell over your legs. Using a fat bar or having a pad on the bar can greatly reduce the discomfort caused by this exercise.
Roll the bar so that it is directly above your hips, and lean back against the bench so that your shoulder blades are near the top of it.

Begin the movement by driving through your feet, extending your hips vertically through the bar. Your weight should be supported by your shoulder blades and your feet. Extend as far as possible, then reverse the motion to return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Step Ups
exercises.formTip: Push through the whole foot on the step and avoid pushing off the back leg.
exercises.notes: Use a box height that keeps your knee at about 90 degrees at the top.
instructions: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).

Place the right foot on the elevated platform. Step on the platform by extending the hip and the knee of your right leg. Use the heel mainly to lift the rest of your body up and place the foot of the left leg on the platform as well. Breathe out as you execute the force required to come up.

Step down with the left leg by flexing the hip and knee of the right leg as you inhale. Return to the original standing position by placing the right foot of to next to the left foot on the initial position.
Repeat with the right leg for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raises
exercises.formTip: Rise fully onto your toes, pause at the top, and lower with control to a full stretch.
exercises.notes: Pause at the bottom of each rep for a deeper stretch.
instructions: Adjust the padded lever of the calf raise machine to fit your height.

Place your shoulders under the pads provided and position your toes facing forward (or using any of the two other positions described at the beginning of the chapter). The balls of your feet should be secured on top of the calf block with the heels extending off it. Push the lever up by extending your hips and knees until your torso is standing erect. The knees should be kept with a slight bend; never locked. Toes should be facing forward, outwards or inwards as described at the beginning of the chapter. This will be your starting position.

Raise your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing your calf. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending at any time. Hold the contracted position by a second before you start to go back down.
Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

workouts.name: Hinge Power & Core
workouts.description: A posterior-chain and core session that complements your push-day recovery. Heavy hinging and single-leg work build strength and stability, while core exercises support your heavier lifts.
workouts.warmup: 5 min rowing or cycling, then 10 Superman holds for 3 seconds, 10 Single Leg Glute Bridges per side, and 2 light sets of Barbell Deadlift with just the bar.
workouts.cooldown: 5 min easy walking, then Cat Stretch for 60 seconds, Child's Pose for 60 seconds, and Oblique Crunches stretch on the floor for 30 seconds per side.

exercises.name: Barbell Deadlift
exercises.formTip: Keep the bar over mid-foot, brace your core, and drive the floor away while keeping your back neutral.
exercises.notes: Reset your setup between reps and stop if form breaks down.
instructions: Stand in front of a loaded barbell.

While keeping the back as straight as possible, bend your knees, bend forward and grasp the bar using a medium (shoulder width) overhand grip. This will be the starting position of the exercise. Tip: If it is difficult to hold on to the bar with this grip, alternate your grip or use wrist straps.

While holding the bar, start the lift by pushing with your legs while simultaneously getting your torso to the upright position as you breathe out. In the upright position, stick your chest out and contract the back by bringing the shoulder blades back. Think of how the soldiers in the military look when they are in standing in attention.

Go back to the starting position by bending at the knees while simultaneously leaning the torso forward at the waist while keeping the back straight. When the weights on the bar touch the floor you are back at the starting position and ready to perform another repetition.
Perform the amount of repetitions prescribed in the program.

exercises.name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.weight: Bodyweight (add a dumbbell on the hips when ready)
exercises.formTip: Keep your hips level and drive through the heel of the working leg.
exercises.notes: Pause at the top for one second on each rep.
instructions: Lay on the floor with your feet flat and knees bent.
Raise one leg off of the ground, pulling the knee to your chest. This will be your starting position.
Execute the movement by driving through the heel, extending your hip upward and raising your glutes off of the ground.
Extend as far as possible, pause and then return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.formTip: Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels and squeeze your glutes.
exercises.notes: Regress to knees if your hips sag.
instructions: Get into a prone position on the floor, supporting your weight on your toes and your forearms. Your arms are bent and directly below the shoulder.
Keep your body straight at all times, and hold this position as long as possible. To increase difficulty, an arm or leg can be raised.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.formTip: Lean back with a straight spine and rotate from the torso, not just the arms.
exercises.notes: Keep your feet down or elevate them for more difficulty.
instructions: Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them. Your legs should be bent at the knees.

Elevate your upper body so that it creates an imaginary V-shape with your thighs. Your arms should be fully extended in front of you perpendicular to your torso and with the hands clasped. This is the starting position.
Twist your torso to the right side until your arms are parallel with the floor while breathing out.
Hold the contraction for a second and move back to the starting position while breathing out. Now move to the opposite side performing the same techniques you applied to the right side.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.formTip: Press your lower back into the floor and extend opposite arm and leg slowly.
exercises.notes: Keep your lower back flat throughout the movement.
instructions: Begin lying on your back with your hands extended above you toward the ceiling.
Bring your feet, knees, and hips up to 90 degrees.

Exhale hard to bring your ribcage down and flatten your back onto the floor, rotating your pelvis up and squeezing your glutes. Hold this position throughout the movement. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the exercise by extending one leg, straightening the knee and hip to bring the leg just above the ground.
Maintain the position of your lumbar and pelvis as you perform the movement, as your back is going to want to arch.
Stay tight and return the working leg to the starting position.
Repeat on the opposite side, alternating until the set is complete.

workouts.name: Full-Body Mobility Flow
workouts.description: A gentle full-body stretch sequence suited to a lightly active beginner. It loosens the spine, shoulders, hamstrings and hip flexors, which helps daily movement and recovery without adding strain to your routine.
workouts.warmup: Stand tall and roll your shoulders backward 10 times, then forward 10 times. March in place for 2 minutes, gradually lifting your knees and swinging your arms, to raise your body temperature.
workouts.cooldown: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Hug both knees gently to your chest for 30 seconds, then rest with your arms relaxed by your sides and breathe slowly for 1 minute.

exercises.name: Cat Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Inhale to arch your back and lift your chest, exhale to round your spine toward the ceiling.
exercises.notes: Move slowly and keep the movement controlled through the whole spine.
instructions: Position yourself on the floor on your hands and knees.
Pull your belly in and round your spine, lower back, shoulders, and neck, letting your head drop.
Hold for 15 seconds.

exercises.name: Upward Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Inhale as you reach up, exhale as you relax your shoulders down.
exercises.notes: Keep your ribs down so you don't overarch the lower back.
instructions: Extend both hands straight above your head, palms touching.
Slowly push your hands up and back, keeping your back straight.

exercises.name: Spinal Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Exhale as you rotate gently, inhale to return to center.
exercises.notes: Rotate from the upper back and avoid forcing the twist.
instructions: Sit in a chair so your back is straight and your feet planted on the floor.
Interlace your fingers behind your head, elbows out and your chin down.
Twist your upper body to one side about 3 times as far as you can. Then lean forward and twist your torso to reach your elbow to the floor on the inside of your knee.
Return to upright position and then repeat for your other side.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Breathe deeply and let each exhale allow a little more length.
exercises.notes: Keep a slight bend in the front knee if you feel tightness.
instructions: Lie on your back with one leg extended above you, with the hip at ninety degrees. Keep the other leg flat on the floor.
Loop a belt, band, or rope over the ball of your foot. This will be your starting position.
Pull on the belt to create tension in the calves and hamstrings. Hold this stretch for 10-30 seconds, and repeat with the other leg.

exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor
exercises.breathingCue: Exhale and gently tuck the pelvis forward as you lean into the stretch.
exercises.notes: Keep your torso upright and squeeze the back glute lightly.
instructions: Kneel on a mat and bring your right knee up so the bottom of your foot is on the floor and extend your left leg out behind you so the top of your foot is on the floor.
Shift your weight forward until you feel a stretch in your hip. Hold for 15 seconds, then repeat for your other side.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.breathingCue: Breathe into your back, letting the ribs expand on each inhale.
exercises.notes: Widen the knees if your hips feel tight.
instructions: Get on your hands and knees, walk your hands in front of you.
Lower your buttocks down to sit on your heels. Let your arms drag along the floor as you sit back to stretch your entire spine.
Once you settle onto your heels, bring your hands next to your feet and relax. "breathe" into your back. Rest your forehead on the floor. Avoid this position if you have knee problems.

workouts.name: Hip and Hamstring Release
workouts.description: This session focuses on the hips, hamstrings and lower back, areas that tighten from sitting for long periods. It is a calm, low-intensity option that supports mobility for a lightly active lifestyle.
workouts.warmup: Walk in place or around the room for 3 minutes at an easy pace. Then perform 10 slow leg swings forward and back on each leg, holding a wall for balance.
workouts.cooldown: Lie on your back and let both knees fall gently to one side for 30 seconds, then switch sides. Finish by resting flat on your back for 1 minute with slow, steady breaths.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Inhale to lengthen the spine, exhale to fold a little further forward.
exercises.notes: Hinge at the hips rather than rounding the lower back.
instructions: Lie on your back with one leg extended above you, with the hip at ninety degrees. Keep the other leg flat on the floor.
Loop a belt, band, or rope over the ball of your foot. This will be your starting position.
Pull on the belt to create tension in the calves and hamstrings. Hold this stretch for 10-30 seconds, and repeat with the other leg.

exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor
exercises.breathingCue: Breathe slowly and steadily, relaxing the hip with each exhale.
exercises.notes: Use a cushion under the kneeling knee if needed.
instructions: Kneel on a mat and bring your right knee up so the bottom of your foot is on the floor and extend your left leg out behind you so the top of your foot is on the floor.
Shift your weight forward until you feel a stretch in your hip. Hold for 15 seconds, then repeat for your other side.

exercises.name: Cat Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Synchronize each movement with a full inhale and exhale.
exercises.notes: Move through the spine one vertebra at a time.
instructions: Position yourself on the floor on your hands and knees.
Pull your belly in and round your spine, lower back, shoulders, and neck, letting your head drop.
Hold for 15 seconds.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.breathingCue: Allow the breath to slow and deepen in the lower back.
exercises.notes: Use a pillow under the chest or hips for support.
instructions: Get on your hands and knees, walk your hands in front of you.
Lower your buttocks down to sit on your heels. Let your arms drag along the floor as you sit back to stretch your entire spine.
Once you settle onto your heels, bring your hands next to your feet and relax. "breathe" into your back. Rest your forehead on the floor. Avoid this position if you have knee problems.

exercises.name: Spinal Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Exhale into each twist and inhale to lengthen.
exercises.notes: Keep hips stacked and avoid pushing into the twist.
instructions: Sit in a chair so your back is straight and your feet planted on the floor.
Interlace your fingers behind your head, elbows out and your chin down.
Twist your upper body to one side about 3 times as far as you can. Then lean forward and twist your torso to reach your elbow to the floor on the inside of your knee.
Return to upright position and then repeat for your other side.

workouts.name: Upper Back and Shoulder Opener
workouts.description: This routine opens the chest, shoulders and upper back, which can feel stiff from desk work or screens. It is gentle and approachable, making it a good fit for a lightly active beginner.
workouts.warmup: Sit tall and perform 10 slow shoulder circles backward, then 10 forward. Follow with 1 minute of gentle marching in place to warm up.
workouts.cooldown: Sit comfortably and clasp your hands behind your back, lifting slightly. Hold for 30 seconds, then relax your arms and breathe slowly for 1 minute.

exercises.name: Upward Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Inhale to lift through the chest, exhale to soften the shoulders.
exercises.notes: Stand tall and keep the neck relaxed.
instructions: Extend both hands straight above your head, palms touching.
Slowly push your hands up and back, keeping your back straight.

exercises.name: Spinal Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Exhale to rotate, inhale to return to center.
exercises.notes: Turn from the mid-back and keep the shoulders relaxed.
instructions: Sit in a chair so your back is straight and your feet planted on the floor.
Interlace your fingers behind your head, elbows out and your chin down.
Twist your upper body to one side about 3 times as far as you can. Then lean forward and twist your torso to reach your elbow to the floor on the inside of your knee.
Return to upright position and then repeat for your other side.

exercises.name: Cat Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Inhale to open the chest, exhale to round the upper back.
exercises.notes: Keep the movement smooth and avoid jerky motions.
instructions: Position yourself on the floor on your hands and knees.
Pull your belly in and round your spine, lower back, shoulders, and neck, letting your head drop.
Hold for 15 seconds.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.breathingCue: Let each exhale sink the shoulders lower toward the floor.
exercises.notes: Reach your arms forward to increase the stretch across the upper back.
instructions: Get on your hands and knees, walk your hands in front of you.
Lower your buttocks down to sit on your heels. Let your arms drag along the floor as you sit back to stretch your entire spine.
Once you settle onto your heels, bring your hands next to your feet and relax. "breathe" into your back. Rest your forehead on the floor. Avoid this position if you have knee problems.

workouts.name: Back and Biceps Strength
workouts.description: A pulling session that builds back thickness and arm strength. Compound rows and pulldowns drive the most muscle growth, and curls add direct biceps volume. Suited to a moderately active lifter building muscle.
workouts.warmup: 5 min light cycling or brisk walking, then 2 sets of 10 band or light cable pull-aparts and 1 light set of each working exercise.
workouts.cooldown: 5 min easy walking, then stretch lats and biceps for 30 seconds each per side.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.formTip: Pull the bar to your upper chest while driving elbows down and slightly back.
exercises.notes: Avoid leaning back excessively or swinging the torso.
instructions: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a wide bar attached to the top pulley. Make sure that you adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height. These pads will prevent your body from being raised by the resistance attached to the bar.

Grab the bar with the palms facing forward using the prescribed grip. Note on grips: For a wide grip, your hands need to be spaced out at a distance wider than shoulder width. For a medium grip, your hands need to be spaced out at a distance equal to your shoulder width and for a close grip at a distance smaller than your shoulder width.

As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position.

As you breathe out, bring the bar down until it touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the full contracted position. The upper torso should remain stationary and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work except for holding the bar; therefore do not try to pull down the bar using the forearms.

After a second at the contracted position squeezing your shoulder blades together, slowly raise the bar back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched. Inhale during this portion of the movement.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Rows
exercises.formTip: Keep your chest tall and pull the handle to your lower ribs, squeezing shoulder blades together.
exercises.notes: Do not round the lower back at the end of the pull.
instructions: For this exercise you will need access to a low pulley row machine with a V-bar. Note: The V-bar will enable you to have a neutral grip where the palms of your hands face each other. To get into the starting position, first sit down on the machine and place your feet on the front platform or crossbar provided making sure that your knees are slightly bent and not locked.
Lean over as you keep the natural alignment of your back and grab the V-bar handles.

With your arms extended pull back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle from your legs. Your back should be slightly arched and your chest should be sticking out. You should be feeling a nice stretch on your lats as you hold the bar in front of you. This is the starting position of the exercise.

Keeping the torso stationary, pull the handles back towards your torso while keeping the arms close to it until you touch the abdominals. Breathe out as you perform that movement. At that point you should be squeezing your back muscles hard. Hold that contraction for a second and slowly go back to the original position while breathing in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.formTip: Brace one hand on a bench and row the dumbbell toward your hip, keeping your torso still.
exercises.notes: Use a neutral spine and avoid twisting the hips.
instructions: Choose a flat bench and place a dumbbell on each side of it.

Place the right leg on top of the end of the bench, bend your torso forward from the waist until your upper body is parallel to the floor, and place your right hand on the other end of the bench for support.

Use the left hand to pick up the dumbbell on the floor and hold the weight while keeping your lower back straight. The palm of the hand should be facing your torso. This will be your starting position.

Pull the resistance straight up to the side of your chest, keeping your upper arm close to your side and keeping the torso stationary. Breathe out as you perform this step. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the full contracted position. Also, make sure that the force is performed with the back muscles and not the arms. Finally, the upper torso should remain stationary and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work except for holding the dumbbell; therefore do not try to pull the dumbbell up using the forearms.
Lower the resistance straight down to the starting position. Breathe in as you perform this step.
Repeat the movement for the specified amount of repetitions.
Switch sides and repeat again with the other arm.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
exercises.formTip: Keep elbows pinned at your sides and curl without swinging your body.
exercises.notes: Control the lowering phase for better muscle stimulus.
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Hammer Curls
exercises.formTip: Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other and keep wrists neutral throughout.
exercises.notes: Finish the set with controlled reps rather than momentum.
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell on each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
The palms of the hands should be facing your torso. This will be your starting position.

Now, while holding your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the weight forward while contracting the biceps. Continue to raise the weight until the biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief moment as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Focus on keeping the elbow stationary and only moving your forearm.
After the brief pause, inhale and slowly begin the lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

workouts.name: Full-Body HIIT Circuit
workouts.description: A short, high-intensity circuit that raises heart rate and adds conditioning to support muscle building and recovery. Bodyweight moves keep it accessible and time-efficient for a moderately active person.
workouts.warmup: 5 min brisk walk or light jog, then 1 minute of arm circles, leg swings and bodyweight squats.
workouts.cooldown: 3 min slow walking followed by deep breathing and gentle chest and hip stretches.

exercises.name: Freehand Jump Squat
exercises.notes: Land softly with knees tracking over toes. Step down if you need to protect your joints.
instructions: Cross your arms over your chest.
With your head up and your back straight, position your feet at shoulder width.
Keeping your back straight and chest up, squat down as you inhale until your upper thighs are parallel, or lower, to the floor.
Now pressing mainly with the ball of your feet, jump straight up in the air as high as possible, using the thighs like springs. Exhale during this portion of the movement.
When you touch the floor again, immediately squat down and jump again.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Pushups
exercises.notes: Keep a straight line from head to heels. Drop to knees if form breaks down.
instructions: Lie on the floor face down and place your hands about 36 inches apart while holding your torso up at arms length.
Next, lower yourself downward until your chest almost touches the floor as you inhale.
Now breathe out and press your upper body back up to the starting position while squeezing your chest.
After a brief pause at the top contracted position, you can begin to lower yourself downward again for as many repetitions as needed.

exercises.name: Mountain Climbers
exercises.notes: Keep hips low and drive knees toward the chest with control.
instructions: Begin in a pushup position, with your weight supported by your hands and toes. Flexing the knee and hip, bring one leg until the knee is approximately under the hip. This will be your starting position.

Explosively reverse the positions of your legs, extending the bent leg until the leg is straight and supported by the toe, and bringing the other foot up with the hip and knee flexed. Repeat in an alternating fashion for 20-30 seconds.

exercises.name: Air Bike
exercises.notes: Move slowly through the torso and keep the lower back neutral.
instructions: Lie flat on the floor with your lower back pressed to the ground. For this exercise, you will need to put your hands beside your head. Be careful however to not strain with the neck as you perform it. Now lift your shoulders into the crunch position.
Bring knees up to where they are perpendicular to the floor, with your lower legs parallel to the floor. This will be your starting position.

Now simultaneously, slowly go through a cycle pedal motion kicking forward with the right leg and bringing in the knee of the left leg. Bring your right elbow close to your left knee by crunching to the side, as you breathe out.
Go back to the initial position as you breathe in.
Crunch to the opposite side as you cycle your legs and bring closer your left elbow to your right knee and exhale.
Continue alternating in this manner until all of the recommended repetitions for each side have been completed.

workouts.name: Full-Body Mobility and Recovery
workouts.description: A gentle session to improve range of motion and speed recovery after strength and HIIT training. It targets areas that tighten with desk work and heavy lifting.
workouts.warmup: 3 min slow walking or marching in place, then gentle arm circles and torso rotations.
workouts.cooldown: Finish with 2 minutes of quiet breathing lying on your back, letting your heart rate settle.

exercises.name: Cat Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Inhale to arch the back, exhale to round the spine.
exercises.notes: Move slowly through the full range on hands and knees.
instructions: Position yourself on the floor on your hands and knees.
Pull your belly in and round your spine, lower back, shoulders, and neck, letting your head drop.
Hold for 15 seconds.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.breathingCue: Breathe slowly into the back of the ribs.
exercises.notes: Walk hands forward to feel a gentle lengthening along the back.
instructions: Get on your hands and knees, walk your hands in front of you.
Lower your buttocks down to sit on your heels. Let your arms drag along the floor as you sit back to stretch your entire spine.
Once you settle onto your heels, bring your hands next to your feet and relax. "breathe" into your back. Rest your forehead on the floor. Avoid this position if you have knee problems.

exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor
exercises.breathingCue: Exhale as you gently shift the hips forward.
exercises.notes: Squeeze the glute of the back leg to deepen the stretch safely.
instructions: Kneel on a mat and bring your right knee up so the bottom of your foot is on the floor and extend your left leg out behind you so the top of your foot is on the floor.
Shift your weight forward until you feel a stretch in your hip. Hold for 15 seconds, then repeat for your other side.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch on each exhale.
exercises.notes: Keep the spine long and stop before any sharp pain.
instructions: Lie on your back with one leg extended above you, with the hip at ninety degrees. Keep the other leg flat on the floor.
Loop a belt, band, or rope over the ball of your foot. This will be your starting position.
Pull on the belt to create tension in the calves and hamstrings. Hold this stretch for 10-30 seconds, and repeat with the other leg.

exercises.name: Spinal Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Inhale to prepare, exhale to rotate gently.
exercises.notes: Rotate from the mid-back and keep the hips grounded.
instructions: Sit in a chair so your back is straight and your feet planted on the floor.
Interlace your fingers behind your head, elbows out and your chin down.
Twist your upper body to one side about 3 times as far as you can. Then lean forward and twist your torso to reach your elbow to the floor on the inside of your knee.
Return to upright position and then repeat for your other side.

exercises.name: Upward Stretch
exercises.breathingCue: Inhale as you reach up and lengthen through the sides of the body.
exercises.notes: Keep shoulders relaxed away from the ears.
instructions: Extend both hands straight above your head, palms touching.
Slowly push your hands up and back, keeping your back straight.

results.note: Sedentary is capped at Beginner: no intermediate or expert exercise, no Advanced workout (handoff 6.3.6).

workouts.name: Beginner Full-Body Strength
workouts.description: Multi-joint, low-impact moves build muscle and raise daily energy use, which supports fat loss. Starting with light loads and controlled reps suits a sedentary beginner and lowers injury risk.
workouts.warmup: 5 min easy walking on the spot or treadmill, then 10 bodyweight squats, 5 incline push-ups, and 10 glute bridges at a comfortable pace.
workouts.cooldown: 5 min slow walking, then hold Child's Pose for 30 seconds and Hamstring Stretch for 30 seconds per side while breathing slowly.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.formTip: Hold the kettlebell close to your chest, keep your heels down, and sit back and down until your thighs are about parallel.
exercises.notes: Use a bodyweight squat if no kettlebell is available.
instructions: Stand holding a light kettlebell by the horns close to your chest. This will be your starting position.
Squat down between your legs until your hamstrings are on your calves. Keep your chest and head up and your back straight.
At the bottom position, pause and use your elbows to push your knees out. Return to the starting position, and repeat for 10-20 repetitions.

exercises.name: Incline Push-Up
exercises.formTip: Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels and lower your chest toward the edge of a sturdy bench or counter.
exercises.notes: Move to a higher surface to make it easier.
instructions: Stand facing bench or sturdy elevated platform. Place hands on edge of bench or platform, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Position forefoot back from bench or platform with arms and body straight. Arms should be perpendicular to body. Keeping body straight, lower chest to edge of box or platform by bending arms.
Push body up until arms are extended. Repeat.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Rows
exercises.formTip: Keep your chest tall and pull the handle to your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together without leaning back.
exercises.notes: Choose a weight that lets you control the return.
instructions: For this exercise you will need access to a low pulley row machine with a V-bar. Note: The V-bar will enable you to have a neutral grip where the palms of your hands face each other. To get into the starting position, first sit down on the machine and place your feet on the front platform or crossbar provided making sure that your knees are slightly bent and not locked.
Lean over as you keep the natural alignment of your back and grab the V-bar handles.

With your arms extended pull back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle from your legs. Your back should be slightly arched and your chest should be sticking out. You should be feeling a nice stretch on your lats as you hold the bar in front of you. This is the starting position of the exercise.

Keeping the torso stationary, pull the handles back towards your torso while keeping the arms close to it until you touch the abdominals. Breathe out as you perform that movement. At that point you should be squeezing your back muscles hard. Hold that contraction for a second and slowly go back to the original position while breathing in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Butt Lift (Bridge)
exercises.formTip: Press through your heels, lift your hips until your body forms a straight line, and squeeze your glutes at the top.
exercises.notes: Avoid arching your lower back at the top.
instructions: Lie flat on the floor on your back with the hands by your side and your knees bent. Your feet should be placed around shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
Pushing mainly with your heels, lift your hips off the floor while keeping your back straight. Breathe out as you perform this part of the motion and hold at the top for a second.
Slowly go back to the starting position as you breathe in.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.formTip: Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your body in one straight line from head to heels.
exercises.notes: Drop to your knees if you cannot hold a straight line.
instructions: Get into a prone position on the floor, supporting your weight on your toes and your forearms. Your arms are bent and directly below the shoulder.
Keep your body straight at all times, and hold this position as long as possible. To increase difficulty, an arm or leg can be raised.

workouts.name: Beginner Steady-State Walk
workouts.description: Steady low-intensity walking burns steady calories with little joint stress, making it a sustainable habit for a sedentary person trying to lose fat.
workouts.warmup: 5 min slow treadmill walk at 3 km/h with gentle arm swings.
workouts.cooldown: 5 min slow walk at 3 km/h, then Hamstring Stretch and Kneeling Hip Flexor, 30 seconds each side.

exercises.name: Walking, Treadmill
exercises.targetHR: 55-65% of max HR (you can talk in full sentences)
exercises.structure: Warm up 5 min, walk 30 min at a steady pace of about 5-6 km/h with a 1% incline if comfortable, then cool down 5 min.
exercises.notes: Increase speed or incline by small amounts each week as fitness improves.
instructions: To begin, step onto the treadmill and select the desired option from the menu. Most treadmills have a manual setting, or you can select a program to run. Typically, you can enter your age and weight to estimate the amount of calories burned during exercise. Elevation can be adjusted to change the intensity of the workout.

Treadmills offer convenience, cardiovascular benefits, and usually have less impact than walking outside. When walking, you should move at a moderate to fast pace, not a leisurely one. Being an activity of lower intensity, walking doesn't burn as many calories as some other activities, but still provides great benefit. A 150 lb person will burn about 175 calories walking 4 miles per hour for 30 minutes, compared to 450 calories running twice as fast. Maintain proper posture as you walk, and only hold onto the handles when necessary, such as when dismounting or checking your heart rate.

workouts.name: Beginner Core and Cardio Intervals
workouts.description: Short work intervals with longer rests keep effort manageable for a beginner while still raising heart rate enough to support fat loss.
workouts.warmup: 3 min easy marching on the spot, then 10 arm circles and 10 slow bodyweight squats.
workouts.cooldown: 3 min easy walking on the spot, then Child's Pose for 30 seconds and Cat Stretch for 30 seconds.

exercises.name: Mountain Climbers
exercises.notes: Start slowly with hands on a stable surface and keep hips level. Reduce speed if form breaks down.
instructions: Begin in a pushup position, with your weight supported by your hands and toes. Flexing the knee and hip, bring one leg until the knee is approximately under the hip. This will be your starting position.

Explosively reverse the positions of your legs, extending the bent leg until the leg is straight and supported by the toe, and bringing the other foot up with the hip and knee flexed. Repeat in an alternating fashion for 20-30 seconds.

exercises.name: Bicycling, Stationary
exercises.notes: Use a light resistance setting and keep a pace where you can still speak in short phrases.
instructions: To begin, seat yourself on the bike and adjust the seat to your height.

Select the desired option from the menu. You may have to start pedaling to turn it on. You can use the manual setting, or you can select a program to use. Typically, you can enter your age and weight to estimate the amount of calories burned during exercise. The level of resistance can be changed throughout the workout. The handles can be used to monitor your heart rate to help you stay at an appropriate intensity.

A recovery day lets muscles repair after Monday's full-body session.
Steady cardio adds extra calorie burn to support fat loss without overloading muscles.
Rest between training days keeps energy up and reduces injury risk.
A second full-body session keeps overall training volume high across the week.
A full rest day before the weekend supports recovery and consistency.
A final rest day prepares you for the week ahead.

days.note: Starts the week with heavy upper-body compound work while fresh, targeting chest, back, and shoulders for muscle growth.
Follows an upper day so legs get fresh stimulus, building quads, hamstrings, and glutes for overall mass.
Recovery day between leg and upper sessions lets muscle repair and supports growth.
Targets chest, shoulders, and triceps after a full rest day, adding volume for hypertrophy.
Trains back and biceps the day after push work, keeping muscle groups from overlapping back to back.
Provides a second recovery day before the weekend, helping prevent overtraining given the high activity level.
Ends the week with leg training after two rest-separated days, balancing the split and building lower-body strength.
